evals.prompt: We're on Supabase and the security advisor export has like 90 items. Can you triage it and tell me which ones actually matter? Don't change anything in prod.
evals.expected_output: Builds the privilege matrix from the live catalog (table and column grants, function EXECUTE, RLS, policies, view security_invoker) instead of trusting the export; classifies advisor items as intended (deny-all tables, guarded definer functions) or real; separately scans owner-visible rows for bearer or counterparty columns the advisor cannot see, proves any hit with a set-role probe in a rolled-back transaction reporting only token length; returns a triage table with evidence and a proposed fix order. No production writes.

evals.prompt: Our password reset and invite flows store a token on the row and the edge function looks it up with .eq('token', token). A user can SELECT their own rows through RLS. Is that a problem? If so fix it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the columns as bearer columns handed to the user they authorize against; proves readability as authenticated with the owner's jwt claims; lists every reader and writer of the tables and flags any hybrid client (service key plus caller Authorization header) or select('*') that the revoke would break; writes a migration that revokes all from anon and authenticated and re-grants display columns by name; dry-runs it in a transaction ending in RAISE EXCEPTION with probes both ways; adds pgTAP assertions and a no-token-column-granted invariant.

evals.prompt: review this migration before I merge: it adds a SECURITY DEFINER function get_member_status(uuid) with REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC, a new table for audit notes, and a public view over listings
evals.expected_output: Checks default privileges and explains that REVOKE FROM PUBLIC leaves named-role EXECUTE grants on platforms that set them, so the revoke must name anon and authenticated; checks the function pins the caller and sets search_path; states whether the new table is auto-granted or born without grants in production versus the CI replay and requires explicit grants (including for the backend role) plus RLS; recommends security_invoker for the view with base-table policy and column grants, proven by hashing its output as anon; proposes pgTAP assertions for each.
